title: Niccolò Guidi di Bagno to the Secretariat of State, Paris, 5 January 1652 (AAV Francia 104; DECODE R5622)

steps.what: Downloaded and inspected all five authenticated DECODE images.
Checked the exact shelfmark and adjacent DECODE records; no same-text or same-key sibling was found.
Tested Lasry's reconstructed Francia 346 key; its mandatory 6 separator is incompatible with R5622's repeated 66 and 666, and a checked line gives malformed groups and no Italian.
Tried whole-line OCR, digit segmentation and glyph clustering on ff. 6r-7v.
Searched exact shelfmark, sender, date and route and checked the Ranuzzi/Acta Nuntiaturae Gallicae lead; no edition of this despatch or online decifrati register was found.

Solved by George Lasry. Transcription was made with CTTS (CrypTool Transcriber and Solver), using its machine-learning model and manual correction. Ciphertext-only cryptanalysis was performed with GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 under Lasry's direction.
Recovered 1/2/4-digit grouping, homophones, marked 04, and partly alphabetical nomenclator.
Italian nunciature vocabulary and repeated local phrases constrained the unknown key without a matching plaintext or historical key.
Rejected a generic null-5 rule; corrected duplicate boxes and touching-digit ligatures against the images instead.
All four cipher pages given edited Italian and full English translation, preserving uncertain code values and gaps.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1759 tokens, 65 types, it-cinquecento order 4: reading -1.969 per letter; random keys -3.761 (z 5.9); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.677 (mean -2.694, z 79.7); annealer on the real text -1.954. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): George Lasry's contributed CTTS transcription (transcription/all.txt), reading edition, edited rows and automatic key application, English translation, and key.txt; all already in the folder

texts.label: R5622, ff. 6r-7v, Paris, 5 January 1652 (George Lasry's contributed solution)
texts.summary: Written from Paris during the Fronde, the despatch concerns opposition to Cardinal Mazarin's return to France: the Parlement's death sentence and 150,000-livre bounty, threats against Mazarin, and an appeal for papal intervention. The nuncio rejects the Parlement's jurisdiction over a cardinal; a speaker tentatively identified as the Duke of Orléans threatens that Mazarin will be killed in his cardinal's robes unless the pope summons or deprives him.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.969; polyphony 0.0; 37 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -1.954
